towns.name: Jennings County

reporting.basis: Actual receipts and disbursements (cash basis), from the Annual Financial Report filed with the Indiana State Board of Accounts through Indiana Gateway
reporting.scope: All county funds, including the sheriff, jail, courts and county roads; money the county collects for other governments is left out

ledger.description: Interest, asset sales, donations and other receipts
Local income, food and beverage, innkeeper, wheel and other local taxes
State-shared taxes and distributions (motor vehicle highway, excise, casino, cigarette and others)
Clerk Of Circuit Court (County Clerk) (County General)

sources.label: Indiana Gateway, 2024 Annual Financial Report data (detailed receipts, disbursements by fund and department, debt)
U.S. Census Bureau 2025 population estimates
U.S. Census Bureau 2024 Gazetteer (map location)
EFF Atlas of Surveillance (police surveillance technology, searched by department)

notes: Actual receipts and disbursements for calendar year 2024, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report (cash basis). Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school corporations with their own taxes, so they are not included. The county collects property and local income taxes for every government in the county and pays them over; that money is left out.

Indiana's chart of accounts has no function codes, so spending is assigned to a service from the department or fund name (a police department or fire fund is public safety, a motor vehicle highway fund roads, a sewage utility fund utilities); spending in other funds with general names counts as general government.
Money the county holds for others or passes through (tax settlements, payroll and clearing accounts, trusts and escrow; $53,026,649 received) is left out.
Borrowing ($1,492,886) is not counted as revenue.
$325,000 of notes and bonds paid off with new borrowing (refinancing) is left out of debt service.
Transfers between funds, purchases of investments and payroll withholdings paid over are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, notes, leases and loans, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Indiana county candidates file campaign finance reports with their county election board, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Indiana yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

Indiana's chart of accounts has no function codes, so spending is assigned to a service from the department or fund name (a police department or fire fund is public safety, a motor vehicle highway fund roads, a sewage utility fund utilities); spending in other funds with general names counts as general government.
Transfers between funds, purchases of investments and payroll withholdings paid over are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, notes, leases and loans, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Indiana local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county election board, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Indiana yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
